directoryStems.mcq-1bc8eeff963dba123317d678: During a goals-of-care discussion with an older person with chronic illnesses, a physician wants to make an individualized recommendation. Which information should guide the options presented?
directoryStems.mcq-a8407f68b88325c137fe00c1: A physician hesitates to discuss prognosis with an older patient because multiple chronic conditions make the course difficult to estimate. Which communication approach follows Hazzard?
directoryStems.mcq-8966eba5741330455527e264: An 82-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer has received palliative care alongside oncologic treatment for six months. Her disease has progressed despite second-line chemotherapy, and her oncologist estimates survival at two to three months. She has been hospitalized twice in the past month. Her family struggles with the limited prognosis, but she says she is tired of treatment and wants comfort at home. Which plan best aligns care with her expressed goals?
directoryStems.mcq-5493182e5108d5c7d6b8ad34: A 79-year-old woman is being assessed for home palliative care after three admissions in four months for heart-failure exacerbations. She has ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF 25%), stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24 mL/min/1.73 m²), and mild cognitive impairment. She takes furosemide 80 mg twice daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, and spironolactone 12.5 mg daily. She lives with her daughter, who works full time. The patient says she wants “no more hospitals,” but her daughter insists on calling emergency services whenever she becomes breathless. What should be done next to address their differing care expectations?
directoryStems.mcq-4229b89d104bb4ec48bfd9c6: An 81-year-old man with severe COPD (FEV1 28% predicted) has been hospitalized three times in six months, lost 20 pounds, and now needs help bathing and dressing. He asks how much time he has left. His daughter interrupts, saying everything will be fine. After acknowledging how difficult the discussion is, what should the clinician do next?
